subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to resolve symlink targets outside the workspace root into sibling `~/.openclaw` directories, and what exact trust boundary should govern that?
rationale: The code change is small, but the product decision changes what private local files may enter prompt context and the current maintainer comment asks for explicit policy rather than reviving the old resolver patch.

options.title: Approve a narrow bootstrap symlink policy
options.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops through a documented wrapper/fs-safe policy, with tests rejecting direct arbitrary `~/.openclaw` paths and unrelated escapes.

options.title: Keep workspace-only reads
options.body: Preserve the current boundary and instead improve doctor/diagnostics so users see why symlinked bootstrap files were skipped.

options.title: Require explicit trusted roots
options.body: Add or reuse an operator-controlled trusted-root setting before any external bootstrap file can be injected.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow bootstrap symlink policy
recommendation.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops through a documented wrapper/fs-safe policy, with tests rejecting direct arbitrary `~/.openclaw` paths and unrelated escapes.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the active related PR and already documented the desired next decision shape on this issue.
